mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and increased borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.1 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO rises > 2%, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS declines > 100k, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.1 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of instances when HOUST declines > 10%, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.1 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5%, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 increase, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
